w: At 318 hectares, this is Slovenia's largest permanent lake, filling the Bohinj Valley inside Triglav National Park in the northwestern Upper Carniola region. Ringed by the peaks of the Julian Alps and fed by glacial meltwater, it stays the calm, deep-water anchor of the national park's western half.
_facts: 318 hectares, the largest permanent lake in Slovenia

w: Slovenia's tenth-largest town grew up on iron: its ironworks and metallurgy industries built the place, spread along the southern face of the Karawanks range against the Austrian border. Known once by its German name, Assling, Jesenice sits as the gateway town where the Alps meet the Karawanks.
s: The ironworks town at the gateway to the Alps
_facts: tenth-largest town in Slovenia

German name Assling

w: A cable car climbs from the shore of Lake Bohinj to 1,537 metres up Vogel, a 1,922-metre peak inside Triglav National Park. In winter the slopes below the summit run one of Slovenia's biggest ski operations; the rest of the year the same cable car delivers alpine views over the lake.
s: A cable car straight up from the lake to the Alps
_facts: 1,922m mountain in the southern Julian Alps, within Triglav National Park

site of the Vogel Ski Resort, one of Slovenia's biggest

w: Built in 1472 to guard the road out of Bovec toward Carinthia, this fort was stormed by Napoleon's troops in 1797, who put cannon on the high ground above it, later the site of Fort Hermann. The Austrians rebuilt it in the late 1800s, only for Italian artillery to wreck Fort Hermann again in 1915.
s: A 1472 fort taken by Napoleon, wrecked in the Isonzo

w: A grassy saddle straddling the Slovenia-Austria border high in the western Karawanks, wedged between Hrusica Peak and Mount Klek above the town of Jesenice. Sheep still graze its slopes the way border passes rarely get used for anything else: a working pasture that happens to double as a frontier.
s: A grassy border pass still grazed by sheep

w: A village stretched between two landmarks: its southern houses sit on the shore of Lake Bohinj, while its northern boundary climbs to the summit of Triglav, Slovenia's highest peak, meeting the settlements of Trenta and Mojstrana at a single tripoint. Few villages claim a national high point as their own back garden.
s: The village stretching from the lake to Triglav
